title: Live queue readiness retry: race guard, announcements and one state source (RF-163 review follow-ups)
acceptance: A card's readiness Retry cannot be overwritten by an older fetch: fetchOne shares the candidate effect's generation guard (or a per-class token), so a candidate change during a retry, or a class removed and re-added, never leaves a stale error or an orphan result.
Screen-reader users hear a retry start and finish: the queue status or the card announces "Checking readiness…" and the outcome, not only aria-busy.

The retrying flag lives in LivePayloadState (for example a refreshing error variant) rather than a separate set the card and the ranking read differently, and fetchOne reuses the effect's fetch-and-map helper.

A card whose retry lands runnable is re-ranked deliberately: either it may take the copper at once (documented), or the queue holds its order until the instructor acts, and the ranking comment says which.
The busy "Checking…" copper button looks busy (not just cursor-progress), so it does not read as an enabled action that does nothing.
